minutes.summary: The Public Access Cable Committee met by Zoom. It discussed whether to meet in person in September, heard the director's report (graduation live-stream audio failure, town hall hybrid meeting equipment, music licensing quote, library story time), and heard the FY20 closing balance. what_happened.line: The committee agreed by show of hands that the chair and director may meet the TC Passios building reuse architect by Zoom about studio space needs.
Members agreed by consensus, with no formal motion, to spend up to a set limit on a new live-stream encoder to replace the old, unreliable one.
Approval of the FY20 financial report was carried over to the next meeting rather than voted.
The director is to gather more quotes for a background music licensing service and bring them to the next meeting.
No regular meeting will be held in August; the next meeting is September 14, with in-person or Zoom format to be decided by email.

why_it_matters: The space the cable studio gets in the reused TC Passios building, and how much of its equipment budget goes to soundproofing, will shape what local meeting broadcasts and public access programming the town can produce.
The encoder spending and the music licensing quote are small purchases from the committee's own funds, but they show how reliable live coverage of town meetings is being paid for.
watch_next: Next meeting on September 14: the financial report vote, more music licensing quotes, and the format decision.
